name: sudo-bash
description: sudo wrapper elevation (the refined -u doctrine). Recall cases must be covered — an elevating wrapper carries a PrivEsc effect, an unmodelled flag-only invocation degrades soundly to ⊤; benign cases must not raise ⊤/conservative.

cases.note: wrapper elevation: sudo with no -u runs the wrapped command as root, so the report must carry a Direct PrivEsc targeting root
wrapper elevation: an explicit literal root target is the same Direct PrivEsc as the implicit case

flag-only wrapper invocation: --version is unmodelled on the privileged wrapper, so the report degrades soundly to ⊤ (accepted false positive, see SECURITY.md Known Risks); pinned as a recall case, not a benign-precision case
wrapper elevation: the #-prefixed UID spelling names root like the bare spellings do, so the report must carry the Direct PrivEsc targeting root

repeated -u is beyond the doctrine (sudo documents value-taking options as single-use; the behavior on violation is not spelled out): the elevation stays certain but over an unresolved target, never a claimed de-elevation
a privilege wrapper over a code-execution sink still elevates: the report carries the Direct PrivEsc targeting root alongside the sink's ⊤
path-qualified privilege wrapper the frontend cannot peel: the wrapped payload is unanalyzable, so the call degrades soundly to ⊤ instead of the KB record's narrow PrivEsc-only binding
inert flag-only invocation: -l lists permissions and runs nothing, so no PrivEsc fires and the consumed command line degrades to ⊤ (accepted false positive, see SECURITY.md Known Risks)
wrapper elevation precision: a bare -g runs the command as the invoking user (man sudo), so no PrivEsc fires and a note explains the group semantics
wrapper elevation precision: the -u target decides (no PrivEsc for a non-root user); the unmodelled group membership is named by a note, not silently dropped
wrapper elevation precision: an explicit non-root target de-elevates (no PrivEsc); the wrapped touch keeps its FSMeta
